From 95707203407c4cf0b7e520a99d6f46d8aed4b57f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Roman Li <Roman.Li@amd.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2022 14:57:34 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] drm/amd/display: Remove redundant dsc power gating from
 init_hw

[Why]
DSC Power down code has been moved from dcn31_init_hw into init_pipes()
Need to remove it from dcn10_init_hw() as well to avoid duplicated action
on dcn1.x/2.x

[How]
Remove DSC power down code from dcn10_init_hw()

Fixes: 8fa6f4c5715c ("drm/amd/display: fixed the DSC power off sequence during Driver PnP")

Reviewed-by: Anthony Koo <Anthony.Koo@amd.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Yang <Eric.Yang2@amd.com>
Acked-by: Alex Hung <alex.hung@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Roman Li <Roman.Li@amd.com>
Tested-by: Daniel Wheeler <daniel.wheeler@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_hw_sequencer.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_hw_sequencer.c
index ad757b59e00e..1dec40db582d 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_hw_sequencer.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_hw_sequencer.c
@@ -1497,13 +1497,6 @@ void dcn10_init_hw(struct dc *dc)
 			link->link_status.link_active = true;
 	}
 
-	/* Power gate DSCs */
-	if (!is_optimized_init_done) {
-		for (i = 0; i < res_pool->res_cap->num_dsc; i++)
-			if (hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control != NULL)
-				hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control(hws, res_pool->dscs[i]->inst, false);
-	}
-
 	/* we want to turn off all dp displays before doing detection */
 	dc_link_blank_all_dp_displays(dc);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_hw_sequencer.c`**
   - Removed the block of code responsible for powering down the DSCs (Display Stream Compressors) during the `dcn10_init_hw` function. This code was checking if the optimized initialization was not done and then iterating through the DSC resources to call the power gating control function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `dcn10_hw_sequencer.c` is directly related to a previous change made in the `dcn31_init_hw` function, where the DSC power down code was moved to the `init_pipes()` function. The removal of the redundant DSC power gating code from `dcn10_init_hw` ensures that there is no duplicated action occurring in both the `dcn10` and `dcn31` initialization processes, thereby streamlining the initialization sequence and preventing potential conflicts or inefficiencies. This change is part of a broader effort to maintain consistency across different hardware versions (dcn1.x/2.x) in the driver code.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the presence of redundant DSC power gating code in the `dcn10_init_hw` function, which was also being handled in the `init_pipes()` function of `dcn31_init_hw`. This duplication could lead to inconsistent power management behavior for DSCs during the initialization process, potentially causing issues with display functionality.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
/* Power gate DSCs */
if (!is_optimized_init_done) {
    for (i = 0; i < res_pool->res_cap->num_dsc; i++)
        if (hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control != NULL)
            hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control(hws, res_pool->dscs[i]->inst, false);
}
```
Reason:
The presence of this redundant DSC power gating code in the `dcn10_init_hw` function conflicts with the same functionality being handled in the `init_pipes()` function of `dcn31_init_hw`. This duplication can lead to inconsistent power management behavior for DSCs during the initialization process, potentially causing issues with display functionality.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-    /* Power gate DSCs */
-    if (!is_optimized_init_done) {
-        for (i = 0; i < res_pool->res_cap->num_dsc; i++)
-            if (hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control != NULL)
-                hws->funcs.dsc_pg_control(hws, res_pool->dscs[i]->inst, false);
-    }
```
Reason:
By removing the redundant DSC power gating code from `dcn10_init_hw`, the patch ensures that DSC power management is handled solely in the `init_pipes()` function of `dcn31_init_hw`, thus preventing any potential conflicts or inconsistent behavior during the initialization process. This leads to a more reliable display functionality.
